Create a file named case_120.inp in the current working directory containing exactly the input deck text provided in the fenced code block, verbatim and without modification.
Run the CalculiX solver on the input file by executing either ccx -i case_120 or ccx case_120 in a Linux shell, using whichever syntax succeeds on the system.
Capture the CalculiX version string by running ccx -v (or an equivalent command such as ccx --version) and store it as a string for later use.
After the solver run completes, read the file case_120.sta and search for a successful termination indicator such as the text JOB COMPLETED to determine whether the analysis succeeded.
If the run did not succeed, identify the failing file and extract the relevant error message or warning from the solver output or log files.
Write a file named results.json in the working directory as a valid JSON object with exactly these keys: solver set to the string calculix, case_id set to the string case_120, status set to the string success or error depending on the outcome, ccx_version set to the captured version string, artifacts set to an empty JSON array, and notes set to a string containing the exact ccx command that was executed, plus if the run failed the error message and the name of the file from which the failure was determined.
Do not alter, add, or remove any physics definitions (elements, nodes, materials, boundary conditions, transforms, steps) from the provided input deck regardless of whether the run succeeds or fails.
